title: Airbus
text: After three years, 10 million lines of code, over 500 hours of testing with 43 advanced sensors, the Airbus UpNext Optimate demonstrator has officially come to a close! With the number of commercial aircraft expected to double in the next 20 years, Airbus UpNext Optimate aimed to make this future safer and more efficient by supporting pilots in their complex missions on the ground and in the air. The demonstrator has paved the way for Airbus to continue pushing the boundaries on pilot-centric smart automation, improved situational awareness and increased digitalisation for the air traffic management ecosystem. Please join us in saying a fond farewell 👋 and a big congratulations to the Airbus UpNext Optimate demonstrator team! 👏 To take a deep dive into the details, check out the full story: https://ow.ly/noLT50ZVUnn
author: Airbus

title: Sachin Jain, Ph.D.
text: 16 years ago today, we showed up late to our own wedding in a judge's living room It started in Pensacola, where Laura Munoz was struggling in air traffic control school and got dropped into my class Naturally, I volunteered to be her study buddy for reasons that were only partly academic Turns out she didn't need my help at all Less than a year later, I proposed When the day came, I flew into New Orleans and changed into my wedding clothes in the backseat of her colleague's car with Laura riding along We walked into that living room late together, which honestly set the tone for the next 16 years In 2014, we both left the service for six-figure jobs as railroad dispatchers It was the first offer instead of the right one, with on-call hours that left us almost no time with our newborn son, Alex Going back in sent us right back to recruiting duty with Laura beside me the whole way Then came our daughter, Chloe, along with the deployments and the homecomings In 2022 we added one more thing to the list when we co-founded a company together We named it ALAC after Adrian, Laura, Alexander and Chloe because our family is the reason we built it For years she held everything together so I could serve and build in aerospace and defense at the same time This year SkillBridge finally let me go all in, which taught me that marrying your co-founder means work never stays at work We clearly never understood the concept of work-life balance, but we understand each other I'm the frog and she's the bunny, which still somehow works Happy 16th anniversary, Laura! ❤️❤️❤️❤️❤️❤️❤️❤️❤️❤️❤️❤️❤️❤️❤️

title: Saildrone
text: Saildrone and NOAA: National Oceanic & Atmospheric Administration intercepted Hurricane Isaias as it intensified to a Category 3 storm in the Gulf of America today. SD-1045, positioned approximately 150 nm south of Pensacola, FL, intercepted Hurricane Isaias from the northern edge and passed directly through the eye of the storm, experiencing winds gusting over 90 knots (103 mph) and waves up to 20 meters (65 feet) high. To the east of the storm, SD-1057 intercepted the storm’s eastern quadrant, approximately 170 nm west of Sarasota. SD-1045 made history in 2021, capturing the world’s first video footage from inside a major hurricane at sea. While sailing through Category 4 Hurricane Sam, it recorded a wind speed of 109.83 knots (126.4 mph), earning a Guinness World Record for the highest wind speed ever measured by an unmanned surface vehicle. SD-1045 has been deployed for every NOAA/Saildrone hurricane mission since 2021, intercepting major hurricanes and tropical storms each season. Measurements of wind, waves, temperature, and other ocean-atmosphere conditions provide NOAA scientists with critical data to better understand how hurricanes intensify and improve forecasts that help coastal communities prepare. Watch this footage captured by SD-1045 as it passed the eye of Hurricane Isaias, amid fierce winds, towering waves, and sea spray. Read more about our longstanding partnership with NOAA and the science behind these missions: https://lnkd.in/epir_Cty Atlantic Oceanographic and Meteorological Laboratory (AOML) Pacific Marine Environmental Laboratory (PMEL)
author: Saildrone
